nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number, and let $\mathrm{SYT}_k(2,1;n)$ be the number of standard Young tableaux with $n$ cells in the $(2,1)$-hook whose first two rows differ in length by $k$. Set $T_{n,k} = \mathrm{SYT}_k(2,1;n) + (-1)^{n+k+1}$ for $n \ge k$ and $T_{n,k} = 0$ for $n < k$, and let $M(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} m_n x^n$ be the generating function of the Motzkin numbers $m_n$. Then in the ring $\mathbb{Z}[[x]]$ of…
nodes.title: Generating function for the adjusted $(2,1)$-hook tableau counts

nodes.summary: Write a path of length $n$ as a sequence of steps $p_0, \dots, p_{n-1}$, each $D$ (down), $F$ (flat) or $U$ (up), encoded as $0$, $1$, $2$. The path ends with an up step if and only if there is a position $i < n$ with $i + 1 = n$ and $p_i = U$.
nodes.title: Characterization of paths ending with an up step

nodes.summary: Write a path of length $n$ as a sequence of steps $p_0, \dots, p_{n-1}$, each $D$ (down), $F$ (flat) or $U$ (up), encoded as $0$, $1$, $2$. The path ends with an up step when it has a last position, that is, some $i < n$ with $i + 1 = n$, and $p_i = U$.
nodes.title: Paths ending with an up step

nodes.summary: Write a path of length $n$ as a sequence of steps $p_0, \dots, p_{n-1}$, each $D$ (down), $F$ (flat) or $U$ (up), encoded as $0$, $1$, $2$. The path has first non-up step $D$ if and only if there is a position $i$ with $p_i = D$ and $p_j = U$ for every $j < i$.
nodes.title: Characterization of paths whose first non-up step is down

nodes.summary: Write a path of length $n$ as a sequence of steps $p_0, \dots, p_{n-1}$, each $D$ (down), $F$ (flat) or $U$ (up), encoded as $0$, $1$, $2$. The path has first non-up step down when there is a position $i$ with $p_i = D$ and $p_j = U$ for every $j < i$. In particular, a path all of whose steps are up steps, including the empty path, does not qualify.
nodes.title: Paths whose first non-up step is down

nodes.summary: Let $T$ assign to each entry $i < n$ a cell $(r_i, c_i)$ with zero-based row $r_i < n$ and column $c_i < n$, and let $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ be the numbers of entries $i$ with $r_i = 0$ and with $r_i = 1$ respectively. For a natural number $k$, $T$ has first-two-row difference $k$ if and only if $\lambda_1 = \lambda_2 + k$.
nodes.title: Characterization of the first-two-row difference

nodes.summary: Let $T$ assign to each entry $i < n$ a cell $(r_i, c_i)$ with zero-based row $r_i < n$ and column $c_i < n$, and let $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ be the numbers of entries $i$ with $r_i = 0$ and with $r_i = 1$ respectively. For a natural number $k$, $T$ has first-two-row difference $k$ when $\lambda_1 = \lambda_2 + k$, that is, when $\lambda_1 - \lambda_2 = k$.
nodes.title: First-two-row difference of a tableau

nodes.summary: Let $T$ assign to each entry $i < n$ a cell $(r_i, c_i)$ with zero-based row $r_i < n$ and column $c_i < n$. Then $T$ lies in the $(2,1)$-hook if and only if for no entry $i$ do both $r_i \ge 2$ and $c_i \ge 1$ hold.
nodes.title: Characterization of tableaux in the $(2,1)$-hook

nodes.summary: Let $T$ assign to each entry $i < n$ a cell $(r_i, c_i)$ with zero-based row $r_i < n$ and column $c_i < n$. Then $T$ lies in the $(2,1)$-hook when no entry occupies a cell whose row is at least $2$ and whose column is at least $1$, that is, when no $i$ has both $r_i \ge 2$ and $c_i \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Tableaux in the $(2,1)$-hook

nodes.summary: Write a path of length $n$ as a sequence of steps $p_0, \dots, p_{n-1}$, and let $s(p_r) \in \{-1, 0, 1\}$ be the vertical displacement of the step $p_r$ (down, flat or up). For a natural number $k$ and positions $i, j < n$, the pair $(i, j)$ is a hump of height $k$ if and only if $i < j$, $s(p_i) = 1$, $s(p_j) = -1$, $s(p_r) = 0$ for every $r$ with $i < r < j$, and $\sum_{r \le i} s(p_r) = k$.
nodes.title: Characterization of Motzkin humps

nodes.summary: Let $p = p_0 p_1 \cdots p_{n-1}$ be a word of length $n$ in the steps $D$, $F$, $U$ (encoded as $0$, $1$, $2$), whose vertical displacements are $-1$, $0$ and $+1$. For $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and positions $i, j \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the pair $(i, j)$ is a hump of height $k$ in $p$ when $i < j$, $p_i = U$, $p_j = D$, every $p_r$ with $i < r < j$ is $F$, and the height after step $i$, that is, the sum of the…
nodes.title: Motzkin hump

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a word of length $n$ in the steps $D$, $F$, $U$, let $k \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $i, j \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Then $(i, j)$ is a peak of height $k$ in $p$ if and only if $(i, j)$ is a hump of height $k$ in $p$ and $j = i + 1$.
nodes.title: Peaks are humps with adjacent endpoints

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a word of length $n$ in the steps $D$, $F$, $U$, let $k \in \mathbb{N}$, and let $i, j \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$. The pair $(i, j)$ is a peak of height $k$ in $p$ when it is a hump of height $k$ in $p$ and $j = i + 1$, that is, when the down step $p_j$ immediately follows the up step $p_i$.
nodes.title: Motzkin peak

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a word of length $n$ in the steps $D$, $F$, $U$ and let $h \in \mathbb{Z}$. Then $p$ satisfies the bounded Motzkin prefix condition for $h$, in which the prefix length $m$ ranges over $\{0, 1, \dots, n\}$, if and only if $p$ is a Motzkin prefix ending at height $h$, in which $m$ ranges over all natural numbers with $m \le n$.
nodes.title: Bounded form of the Motzkin prefix condition

nodes.summary: Let $p = p_0 p_1 \cdots p_{n-1}$ be a word of length $n$ in the steps $D$, $F$, $U$ (encoded as $0$, $1$, $2$), whose vertical displacements are $-1$, $0$ and $+1$, and let $h \in \mathbb{Z}$. The word $p$ satisfies the bounded Motzkin prefix condition for $h$ when, for every $m \in \{0, 1, \dots, n\}$, the sum of the displacements of $p_0, \dots, p_{m-1}$ is nonnegative, and the sum of the displacements of all $n$…
nodes.title: Bounded Motzkin prefix condition

nodes.summary: Let $p = p_0 p_1 \cdots p_{n-1}$ be a word of length $n$ in the steps $D$, $F$, $U$, whose vertical displacements are $-1$, $0$ and $+1$, and let $h \in \mathbb{Z}$. Then $p$ is a Motzkin prefix ending at height $h$ if and only if, for every natural number $m \le n$, the sum of the displacements of $p_0, \dots, p_{m-1}$ is nonnegative, and the sum of the displacements of all $n$ steps is $h$.
nodes.title: Unfolding the Motzkin prefix condition

nodes.summary: Let $p = p_0 p_1 \cdots p_{n-1}$ be a word of length $n$ in the steps $D$, $F$, $U$ (encoded as $0$, $1$, $2$), whose vertical displacements are $-1$, $0$ and $+1$, and let $h \in \mathbb{Z}$. The word $p$ is a Motzkin prefix ending at height $h$ when, for every natural number $m \le n$, the sum of the displacements of $p_0, \dots, p_{m-1}$ is nonnegative, and the sum of the displacements of all $n$ steps is $h$.
nodes.title: Motzkin prefix

nodes.summary: Let $T$ assign to each entry $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ a cell $T(i) = (r_i, c_i)$ with row and column indices in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Then $T$ is a standard Young tableau of order $n$ if and only if $T$ is injective and, for every entry $i$ and every cell $(r, c)$ with $r \le r_i$ and $c \le c_i$, there is an entry $j \le i$ with $T(j) = (r, c)$.
nodes.title: Unfolding the standard Young tableau condition

nodes.summary: A standard Young tableau of order $n$ is encoded by a map $T$ that assigns to each entry $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ a cell $T(i) = (r_i, c_i)$ with row and column indices in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. The map $T$ is a standard Young tableau when it is injective and, for every entry $i$ and every cell $(r, c)$ with $r \le r_i$ and $c \le c_i$, there is an entry $j \le i$ with $T(j) = (r, c)$.
nodes.title: Standard Young tableau

nodes.summary: Let $p = p_0 p_1 \cdots p_{n-1}$ be a word of length $n$ in the steps $D$, $F$, $U$. Then the last non-flat step of $p$ is $U$ if and only if there is a position $i$ with $p_i = U$ such that $p_j = F$ for every position $j > i$.
nodes.title: Characterization of words whose last non-flat step is up

nodes.summary: A word $p = p_0 p_1 \cdots p_{n-1}$ of length $n$ in the steps $U$ (up), $F$ (flat) and $D$ (down) has last non-flat step up when some position $i$ has $p_i = U$ and every later step $p_j$ with $j > i$ is $F$. In particular, such a word contains an up step.
nodes.title: Paths whose last non-flat step is up

nodes.summary: Use the steps $U = (1,1)$, $F = (1,0)$ and $D = (1,-1)$, and call a word in these steps a Motzkin prefix if none of its initial segments ends below height $0$. For every natural number $n$ there is a bijection between the set of pairs $(k, p)$, where $k$ is a natural number with $k + 2 \le n$ and $p$ is a Motzkin prefix of length $n$ ending at height $k$ whose first step other than $U$ exists and is $D$, and the…
nodes.title: A bijection between first-down and even-height last-up Motzkin prefixes

nodes.summary: Use the steps $U = (1,1)$, $F = (1,0)$ and $D = (1,-1)$, and call a word in these steps a Motzkin prefix if none of its initial segments ends below height $0$. For a natural number $n$, this is the set of pairs $(k, p)$ where $k$ is a natural number with $k \le n - 2$ and $p$ is a Motzkin prefix of length $n$ ending at height $k$ whose first step other than $U$ exists and is $D$.
nodes.title: Motzkin prefixes whose first non-up step is down

nodes.summary: Let $H_{n,k}$ be the number of pairs $(P, h)$ where $P$ is a Motzkin path of length $n$ and $h$ is a hump of height $k$ in $P$, that is, an up step and a later down step with only flat steps between them, where the up step ends at height $k$. Then $H_{4,1} = 8$.

A hump of height $k$ in such a path is a pair consisting of an up step and a later down step with only flat steps between them, where the up step ends at height $k$. A Motzkin prefix of length $n$ ending at height $h$ is a word of $n$ steps that never goes below height $0$ and ends at height $h$; a Motzkin path is a Motzkin prefix ending at height $0$. nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 2$ and $k \ge 1$. A Motzkin path of length $n$ is a sequence of $n$ steps, each up ($+1$), flat ($0$) or down ($-1$), whose partial sums are all nonnegative and whose total is $0$. A hump at height $k$ of such a path is a pair of positions $i < j$ such that step $i$ is up, step $j$ is down, every step strictly between them is flat, and the sum of the steps up to and including step $i$ equals $k$; a peak…

nodes.summary: Use the steps $U = (1,1)$, $F = (1,0)$ and $D = (1,-1)$, and call a word in these steps a Motzkin prefix if none of its initial segments ends below height $0$. For a natural number $n$, this is the set of pairs $(k, p)$ where $k$ is a natural number with $1 \le k \le \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ and $p$ is a Motzkin prefix of length $n$ ending at height $2k$ that contains a $U$ after which every step is $F$.

nodes.summary: The Motzkin series is the formal power series $M(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} m_n x^n$ in $\mathbb{Z}[[x]]$, where $m_n$ is the $n$-th Motzkin number.

nodes.summary: The three Motzkin steps are encoded as $0 = D$ (down), $1 = F$ (flat) and $2 = U$ (up). The height change of the step encoded by $s \in \{0, 1, 2\}$ is the integer $s - 1$; thus $D$ changes the height by $-1$, $F$ by $0$ and $U$ by $+1$.

nodes.summary: The number $\mathrm{SYT}_1(2,1;2)$ of standard Young tableaux of order $2$ in the $(2,1)$-hook whose first row is longer than its second row by exactly $1$ equals $0$.
nodes.title: Hook tableaux of order 2 with row difference 1

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$, $\mathrm{SYT}_k(2,1;n)$ is the number of standard Young tableaux of order $n$ whose shape $\lambda$ lies in the $(2,1)$-hook, that is $\lambda_3 \le 1$, and whose first two row lengths satisfy $\lambda_1 = \lambda_2 + k$ (a missing row has length $0$).
nodes.title: Standard Young tableaux in the $(2,1)$-hook with given row difference

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, let $T$ assign to each entry $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ a cell $T(i)$, given by a zero-based row index and a zero-based column index, both in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. For a natural number $r$, the length of row $r$ is the number of entries $i$ whose cell $T(i)$ lies in row $r$.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
